title: Dedicated Staged Rollouts (Reserved Pools) — Beta Customer Selection + CS Plan
content:
Doc status: working draft (CS planning). Not customer-facing.

Owner: Rachel Kim (Enterprise CS)
Last updated: 2025-02-06

Context
Dedicated staged rollouts for reserved pools is moving from internal dogfood to a limited enterprise beta (2–3 customers). CS needs a shortlist + enablement/comms plan that is realistic given SRE/security constraints and the current limitations (gates + approvals v1, deterministic staged rollout only).

Primary objectives for beta (customer-success lens)
1) Reduce rollout-caused incidents in Dedicated pools by making changes incremental with explicit gates + holds.
2) Validate enterprise governance requirements: approvals, audit trail, and “who changed what when” usability.
3) Build repeatable enablement: onboarding checklist, baseline dashboards, success playbook, and escalation path.
4) Collect hard evidence for GA readiness: fewer latency spikes, fewer support escalations, faster recovery on regressions.

Non-goals for beta (set expectations)
- Not a full experimentation system (no bandits; A/B is separate).
- Not self-serve for all Dedicated tenants; initial access is operator-led and allowlisted.
- Not guaranteed to support quality gating for every workload (optional / limited signals).

Selection criteria (what we want in beta customers)
Must-have
- Dedicated reserved pool (or multiple pools) with active model/runtime/config changes at least monthly.
- Clear pain today: incidents or near-misses during pool-level “all-at-once” rollouts.
- Willingness to run at least 2 staged rollouts during beta window.
- Has an identified engineering owner + on-call contact on the customer side.
- Comfortable with a feature-flagged / allowlisted beta and weekly check-ins.

Nice-to-have
- Compliance/change-management requirements (approvals + audit logs are a key value prop).
- Workload is stable enough to detect regressions (consistent traffic patterns).
- Can support a shadow or low-risk route for Stage 0 / early stage validation.

Avoid (for beta)
- Extremely bursty traffic with poor observability (hard to gate deterministically).
- Customers demanding custom gating beyond the default set for beta, before we have confidence.
- Pools already near saturation with minimal headroom (higher chance of false positives / holds).

Shortlist (recommended)
We are recommending 2 beta customers + 1 backup/alternate.

Candidate A (Recommended): “Northwind Finance” (HS:company_18441)
- Segment: Enterprise fintech
- Why now: Strong compliance asks + explicit request for audit trail of approvals. High value for validating approvals/audit logs.
- Known tickets: SUP-3981 (audit trail), prior escalation notes in HS.
- Risk: Very sensitive to SLA; any gating instability will be high-friction.

Candidate B (Recommended): “Helio Support Platform” (HS:company_19107)
- Segment: Mid-market SaaS (support automation)
- Why now: Has experienced rollout confusion + latency spikes; motivated; faster iteration.
- Known tickets: SUP-3917 (latency spikes), SUP-3924 (traffic split confusion).
- Risk: Can be noisy traffic; we need to ensure evaluation windows are tuned.

Candidate C (Backup): “Aster Research Tools”
- Segment: AI-native startup
- Why: Tech-savvy, willing to dogfood; good for rapid feedback on UI + API behaviors.
- Risk: Less governance/compliance value; may push for self-serve too early.

Decision notes (as of 2025-02-06)
- Proceed with A + B if SRE signs off on headroom/guardrails readiness for their pool sizes.
- Keep C warm as backup if A procurement/security review slows down.

Customer-by-customer detail

1) Northwind Finance (HS:company_18441) — Recommended
Customer goal (their words, paraphrased)
- “We need a defensible change-management trail for model updates and the ability to stop a bad rollout before it impacts the entire reserved pool.”

Current state
- Dedicated reserved pool; strict latency SLOs; customer audits change control quarterly.
- Today’s rollout behavior is effectively pool-level; they currently coordinate changes via manual runbooks and internal approvals.

Why they’re a good beta fit
- High pain + high willingness to invest time.
- Approvals + audit logs are not “nice-to-have”; they will validate real enterprise needs.

Primary risks / watch-outs
- Security review scrutiny: beta language must be tight; avoid implying GA-level guarantees.
- Expectation risk: they may want per-route/per-model sophistication or more gate types.
- Low tolerance for false-positive holds if metrics are flaky.

Required enablement (what CS + Eng must do)
Pre-beta checklist (owner in parentheses)
- Confirm allowlist + feature flag enabled for tenant and pool IDs (Connor O’Brien / Ethan Park).
- Validate audit log export path: ensure rollout events show up in their export destination (Kevin Osei / Marcus Lin).
- Baseline dashboards shared: pool p95 latency, 5xx, timeouts, queue depth, utilization; plus “gate evaluator health” (Allison Grant / Sean Gallagher).
- Dry run in staging or non-prod route (if available) to validate state machine + approvals flow (Leila Farouk / Dev Patel).
- Define initial rollout template with them:
  - Stages: 5% -> 25% -> 100%
  - Evaluation window: 20–30 min (tune based on traffic)
  - Gates: p95 latency, error rate, timeouts, queue depth, GPU utilization (defaults; tuned thresholds signed off by SRE)

Success criteria (Northwind-specific)
- Execute 2 staged rollouts end-to-end (including at least one manual approval step) with no customer-reported SLA breach.
- At least one “pause/hold” event is either triggered correctly (by gate) OR simulated and understood by their on-call.
- Audit trail validation: customer confirms they can answer:
  - who approved each stage
  - timestamps
  - plan version / what changed
- Customer rates confidence improvement >= 8/10 vs current process (qualitative but we’ll capture it).

Comms plan
- Kickoff call (60 min): CS + Product + SRE present. Focus: governance + safety model; confirm what beta is/isn’t.
- Weekly 30 min check-in during rollout windows.
- Provide a one-page “beta operating guide” (internal draft first; then share externally once Security signs off).

Named owners
- CS: Rachel Kim (primary), Miguel Santos (backup)
- Product: Lauren Bishop (Dedicated requirements), Paula Mendes (policy/gates)
- SRE: Sean Gallagher
- Security: Marcus Lin

Next steps
- Rachel to confirm customer-side engineering owner + preferred rollout window.
- Sean to confirm recommended default thresholds are acceptable given their baseline utilization/headroom.


2) Helio Support Platform (HS:company_19107) — Recommended
Customer goal
- “Make traffic splits predictable during model updates so we don’t see surprise queuing / latency spikes.”

Current state
- Dedicated reserved pool with spiky weekday traffic.
- Prior confusion about “how much traffic is actually on the new model” during changes; has resulted in escalations.

Why they’re a good beta fit
- Motivated by recent pain; expects to run multiple rollouts quickly.
- Good candidate for validating Console UX: stage status, gate visualization, and the approvals modal.

Primary risks / watch-outs
- Traffic variability could produce noisy metrics (risk of holds). Need careful evaluation windows.
- They may interpret “25% stage” as “25% of requests” vs deterministic allocation nuances (we need to explain how deterministic hashing works at a conceptual level).

Required enablement
- Same allowlist + feature flag steps.
- Strong emphasis on “metrics freshness” and what happens if gates can’t evaluate (fail-safe hold).
- Setup a “known-good baseline window” for comparison (capture 7-day baseline before first rollout if possible).
- Ensure on-call understands abort vs rollback vs hold semantics.

Success criteria (Helio-specific)
- Execute 3 rollouts (can be smaller changes):
  - 1 model version bump
  - 1 runtime/config change
  - 1 rollback/abort drill (planned)
- Reduce rollout-related support escalations to zero during beta window.
- Customer can self-diagnose (with our dashboards) why a stage is paused at least once (goal: reduce CS/SRE time).

Comms plan
- Kickoff with CS + Console product lead (Marissa Cole) to ensure UI expectations are set.
- Provide a “rollout runbook excerpt” customized for their environment (what to check when paused).

Named owners
- CS: Miguel Santos (primary), Rachel Kim (backup)
- Product: Marissa Cole
- SRE: Rafael Mendes (backup contact)

Next steps
- Miguel to schedule kickoff + gather their current change cadence and top 2 pain points.
- Dev Patel to align support escalation expectations (what constitutes P1 during beta, hours of coverage).


3) Aster Research Tools — Backup
Customer goal
- “We want safer incremental deploys but don’t need heavy governance.”

Why keep them as backup
- Quick to test; tolerant of rough edges; strong technical partner.

Risk
- Less signal on approvals/audit value; more likely to ask for self-serve controls.

Enablement
- Similar, but lighter comms; use as a UX feedback channel and API contract validation.

Success criteria
- Validate API/Console usability + determinism explanation; at least one pause-on-missing-metrics scenario handled cleanly.


Risk assessment (overall beta)
Top risks
1) Gate evaluator reliability / metrics freshness issues cause frequent holds (customer trust hit).
2) Confusion about deterministic allocation (“why did a particular user consistently hit the new model?”).
3) Approvals/audit logs don’t meet enterprise expectations (missing fields, retention, export).
4) Capacity headroom: staged rollouts inadvertently saturate a reserved pool (esp. during 25% -> 100% transition).

Mitigations
- Only onboard pools that pass SRE “headroom check” before first rollout.
- Provide a concise customer explainer for deterministic routing and what ‘percentage’ means.
- Establish explicit “beta operating hours” + escalation policy (who to page, when).
- Do a planned abort/rollback drill with at least one customer (so it’s not learned during an incident).


Beta operating model
Support + escalation
- During active rollout windows: dedicated Slack/bridge on Redwood side (CS + on-call SRE on standby if high-risk window).
- P1 criteria: sustained elevated queue depth, p95 latency breach, 5xx spike, or stuck rollout state.
- If evaluator health degrades: default posture is hold (stop-the-line). Customer is notified that advancement is paused pending metrics recovery.

Cadence
- Weekly customer check-ins (30 min).
- Internal beta standup (15 min) during weeks with active customer rollouts: CS + Product + SRE.

Artifacts we need ready before first customer rollout
- “Beta operator guide” (customer-facing, sanitized).
- “Paused rollout” runbook excerpt + dashboard links.
- A minimal FAQ: approvals, audit logs, hold vs abort, what to do when metrics are missing.


Timeline (CS view)
- Week 0: Confirm candidates + get internal sign-offs (SRE/security/product).
- Week 1: Kickoff calls + environment validation + baseline metrics.
- Weeks 2–4: Execute rollouts (2–3 per customer depending on change cadence).
- Week 5: Beta review + GA readiness feedback: what blocked adoption, what increased confidence.


Open questions / blockers
1) How will we message “automatic rollback” in beta? (Is it enabled by default or only manual abort/rollback?) Need crisp language.
2) What exact audit event fields are guaranteed in beta exports (retention, latency to export)? Security to confirm.
3) Do we require customers to have a dedicated non-prod pool/route for early stage testing, or can Stage 1 be “real prod at 5%” only?
4) Threshold defaults: do we ship SRE defaults per pool size, or require a baseline period first?

Appendix: talk track (internal)
- “This beta is primarily about safety + governance in reserved pools. The system is designed to pause rather than guess when data is missing. We’ll start with conservative stages and tune windows/thresholds based on your baseline.”
